findings.finding: On 2026-08-31, two months into the quarter, Herbalife reaffirmed Q3 guidance unchanged (net sales +0.5% to +4.5% reported, adj. EBITDA $160-180m) with the CFO saying the outlook is 'firmly on track' and that it expects a fifth consecutive quarter of y/y net sales growth; a mid-quarter reaffirmation with roughly 60 days of the quarter's data lowers the odds of a reported-quarter revenue miss below the $1,280m floor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 net sales landed at the top of guidance and adj. EBITDA near the top, and the stock fell 8.65% (2026-08-05); Q1 2026 beat revenue ($1.32B vs $1.30B) and EPS and fell 11.86% (2026-05-06). This name has sold in-guide or above-guide quarters this year.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and largely priced: a revenue print inside the guide is what the company told the market to expect. What is not fully priced is the low probability of a bottom-of-range outcome; if the market doubted the quarter the stock would not be up ~16% since Q2 with almost no puts open (put/call OI 0.02).
findings.independence: Released the same morning as the CEO transition announcement (https://ir.herbalife.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/955/herbalife-announces-planned-ceo-transition), so partly a reassurance device; shares no document with the other findings except the guide numbers used in the bar.

findings.finding: The Q3 reported guide was struck at average rates of the first two weeks of July 2026; through the quarter the dollar was flat to weaker against those rates (DXY ~101 in early July, 99.55 at end-August, 98.61 on 2026-09-09, ~101 again by 2026-09-25; USD/INR in a 95.2-95.7 band against ~95.2 in early July; MXN ~17.0), so the reported line is unlikely to carry more FX headwind than the ~100 bp and $5m EBITDA already in the guide, and may carry a little less.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was the stated cause of the FY adj. EBITDA guide cut (from $675-705m to $670-690m reported) on 2026-08-05, a print the stock sold 8.65%; an FX-driven shortfall has been punished, an FX-neutral quarter has no history here.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model HLF on constant-currency guidance and the company's reported translation, not on a quarter-average FX recalculation; if the market had priced a reported-line tailwind the consensus revenue would sit at the top of the guide rather than near the midpoint ($1.30-1.32B against $1,280-1,331m).
findings.independence: Proxy, macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. INR path from https://newsonair.gov.in/rupee-depreciates-by-34-paise-against-us-dollar/ (2026-09-10, 95.45) and https://dailypioneer.com/news/slug-lite/rupee-falls-12-paise-to-close-at-rs-95-74-against-us-dollar?year=2026 (2026-09-24, 95.74); MXN from https://www.monex.com.mx/portal/download/reportes/AlCierre%20202608013%20ing.pdf (17.03 on 2026-08-13).

findings.finding: India's GST on nutraceuticals fell from 18% to 5% effective 2025-09-22, driving a record ~$250m India Q4 2025 and India growth of +33% reported / +47% cc on +45% volume in Q2 2026; the lap begins 2025-09-22 so the Q4 2026 guide given in this release must absorb the full anniversary of India (~20% of company sales) while China fell 29% cc and EMEA 5.6% cc in Q2, and the FY guide already implies Q4 near +1% at the Q3 midpoint, leaving little room if India decelerates sharply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has decided this stock's prints: Q4 2025 (2026-02-18, +18.32%) and Q3 2025 (2025-11-05, +11.65%) came with growth guides the market bought; Q2 2026 (-8.65%) came with an FX-driven FY EBITDA cut; Q1 2026 (-11.86%) was sold despite a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Earnings Whispers preview names the GST anniversary as the bear case. What is not visible in the price is the size of the comparison: if the market expected a soft Q4 guide the stock would not be up ~16% since the last print with sentiment rising and nearly no puts open; consensus FY revenue of $5.20B already sits in the lower half of the $5.16-5.31B range, which is the one place it shows.
findings.independence: India Q4 2025 ~$250m record and ~$11m transition charge from the Q4 2025 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-2-19-herbalife-nutrition-ltd-stock/); Q2 2026 India +33% / volume +45% and the lap timing from https://finviz.com/news/407924/herbalifes-india-engine-meets-its-gst-anniversary-as-street-bets-on-46-eps-growth (2026-10-26). Net of the rest: North America (+0.2%) and Latin America (+8.2% cc) plus the July launches (Bioniq GO, Helio, Activate Energy) in their first full quarter would have to carry growth; they are about 40% of sales and growing low-to-mid single digits, not enough to fully offset an India that goes from +45% volume to flat.

findings.finding: Ex-India the core is shrinking: in Q2 2026 China net sales fell 24.5% reported / 29.0% cc (third straight quarter of worsening, payoff pushed to 2027), EMEA fell 5.6% cc on a ~12% volume drop and North America grew 0.2%, so Q3 growth rests on Asia Pacific (+23.1% cc) and Latin America; any softening there shows up as a low-end reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print carried the same regional mix (top-of-guide total, China -25%) and was sold 8.65%; the market has punished narrowness even inside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the regional table is public and the reaffirmed guide already contains it; the residual is that the street's revenue consensus sits near the midpoint rather than the low end, which would look different if the market expected China/EMEA to deteriorate further.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with the India finding's growth numbers but is a different line (reported quarter, not the Q4 guide). Earnings Whispers preview makes the same bear case independently: https://finviz.com/news/407924/herbalifes-india-engine-meets-its-gst-anniversary-as-street-bets-on-46-eps-growth

findings.finding: This is the first print and the first forward guide under an interim CEO: Stephan Gratziani stepped down 2026-10-31 with no permanent successor named (board search committee), CFO John DeSimone became interim CEO 2026-11-01 while already announced to retire as CFO on 2026-12-31 with Scott Schaefer succeeding him 2027-01-01, so the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing are set by a transitional team with an incentive to be conservative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under interim leadership in the baseline's eight; the CFO-transition announcement came the same afternoon as the Q2 print that was sold 8.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition is public; what is unpriced is its effect on the tone of the guide, which is an inference. If the market expected a conservative reset, the stock would not have rallied ~16% since the last print.
findings.independence: CFO retirement and successor from the 2026-08-05 CFO release https://ir.herbalife.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/951/herbalife-announces-planned-cfo-transition. Inference, not a document about the guide.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 the board authorized a $250m three-year buyback, about 18% of the ~$1.38B market cap (104.8m shares at $13.21), with the CFO calling repurchases 'a compelling use of capital'; the Q3 release and call can show the first purchases and a pace, against only $10.0m repurchased in H1 2026 and net leverage of 2.2x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline carried a buyback of this size; the April 2026 refinancing print (2026-04-14, +7.34% intraday) is the closest capital-structure event and was bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is priced; the execution pace is not disclosed until this release. If the market expected aggressive buying the stock would not still sit 34% below its 52-week high at under 2x net leverage.
findings.independence: H1 2026 repurchase cash of $10.0m and share count from the Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001180262/000119312526335172/hlf-20260630.htm; leverage from the Q2 release.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is split: Chartmill shows $0.62 and another aggregator $0.63, while Earnings Whispers carries $0.73 consensus and a $0.76 whisper (46% growth on Q3 2025's ~$0.50); arithmetic from the guided $170m EBITDA midpoint, ~$37m quarterly interest after the April refinancing and a ~35% tax rate gives about $0.60, so a guide-midpoint quarter reads as a miss against the higher bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.51 included a $0.14 tax-rate drag and a $0.04 FX drag and was sold 8.65%; Q1 2026's EPS beat ($0.64 vs $0.61) was sold 11.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: Capped small because the bar itself is disputed between sources. If the market's real bar were $0.73, the guide-implied ~$0.60 would already have shown up as estimate cuts; it has not in the aggregator that carries $0.73.
findings.independence: Lower bar from https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/HLF/estimates ($0.62 on $1.32B); guidance inputs from the 2026-08-31 reaffirmation. My EPS arithmetic is inference.

findings.finding: Herbalife has landed at or above the top of its revenue guide in each of the last two quarters (Q1 2026 $1.32B vs $1.30B consensus; Q2 2026 $1,326.8m, +5.4%, top of guide and adj. EBITDA $166.6m toward the upper end), so a Q3 print near $1.33B, about 1% above the $1.31-1.32B consensus, is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both of those top-of-guide quarters were sold, -11.86% and -8.65%, so this line has not paid on this name; sized near zero for that reason.
findings.why_not_priced: A habitual small beat is what the street expects of a company that guides conservatively, so most of it is in the price; consensus sitting near the midpoint rather than the top is the residual.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 beat from https://www.pharmaceuticalprocessingworld.com/herbalife-1q-results-beat-analysts-expectations/ ; shares the Q2 release with the China/EMEA finding.
